sources.dataset: Transmission lines by voltage class (500, 230, 100–161, under 100 kV, not listed)
sources.publisher: HIFLD and OpenStreetMap (ODbL), both named on the story page
sources.cycle: Snapshot; irregular (build years on the map are estimates)
sources.issue: Lines with estimated years are faded on the timeline. Some lines have no voltage class.
sources.next_step: Record which copy and date the map uses. Document how build years were estimated. Add an "estimated" flag in popups.
sources.map_note: Map file: HIFLD Electric Power Transmission Lines (copy and download date not recorded); in-service years from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) for about 25% of line-miles, the rest estimated. The "69 kV and below" class holds 869 lines at 69 kV, 3 at 46 kV and 417 with no voltage.

sources.dataset: Coal ash: Kingston (2008 spill) and Allen ash ponds (Memphis)
sources.publisher: EPA; TVA; Tennessee environment department (TDEC); USGS and University of Memphis (Allen groundwater study)
sources.cycle: Kingston: cleanup complete, monitoring after. Allen: closure and groundwater work ongoing
sources.issue: The two sites sit hundreds of miles apart (Kingston in Roane County, East Tennessee; Allen in Southwest Memphis). Claims about Allen conflict: TVA says the Memphis Sand aquifer is not affected, while a 2018 USGS and University of Memphis study found the shallow aquifer is connected to it.
sources.next_step: Pull TDEC and TVA closure documents and the 2018 USGS and University of Memphis report. Confirm where the Allen ash has gone and its current status. Put both sites on the map with dates and sources.

sources.dataset: Water withdrawals (Memphis Sand Aquifer, cooling use)
sources.publisher: TDEC; MLGW; Protect Our Aquifer
sources.issue: No single public ledger of the draw.
sources.next_step: Request MLGW water-sales records. Find USGS water-use data.

sources.dataset: Rivers, aquifer and watershed: USGS groundwater levels and maps for the Memphis aquifer
sources.publisher: USGS, with the City of Memphis and MLGW; University of Memphis CAESER

sources.next_step: Pick the DeSoto County and Shelby County wells nearest the Colossus sites from SIM 3415 table 1 and record their IDs. Look up USGS stream and watershed datasets separately. Ask MLGW for water-sales data (see records requests).
